features.lt: Streamable HTTP transport only for the registry service; stdio discovery is local-worker-only by design.
Run/project binding is enforced only when a project-owner lookup is provided; absent lookup = PROJECT_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE (fail closed).
Health = initialize+tools/list latency probe; no background prober (on-demand only).
Wrappers only (no schema authoring from scratch); the source tool's own grant is still required at call time.
Plain-text content; no execution of skill content (they are prompts/runbooks by design).
Curated bundled catalog only: no third-party publishing, submissions, payments, or remote registry protocol. Uninstall/update/revoke are implemented and tested.

features.capability: Namespaced slash commands or task commands
features.lt: The chat-surface '/' parser is a client-UI concern outside A5; the registry provides the namespaced, collision-free command store. User-created commands live in the 'team' namespace; plugin namespaces are reserved for catalog content.
No retry/backoff queue (deliberate: no broker exists yet); targets validated by URL policy at creation and re-checked at dispatch.
Team-wide policy only (no per-project policy rules yet); patterns are name-prefix wildcards, not regex, by design.
Python SDK only (a TS client remains future work); no SDK versioning policy document yet.
Notion adapter itself NOT implemented (OAuth + live account unverifiable here) — documented adapter point instead. Sync is pull-only (no webhook/push ingestion).

features.capability: Customer-facing API documentation and SDK distribution
features.lt: No publication to a package index (no index authority in this environment): wheel-install verification is the strongest available proof. No TS SDK docs yet.

features.capability: Slack task intake and status updates
features.lt: No live Slack workspace hit (no credentials in this environment): transport contract validated against real-shape fake servers only. Slash-command surface not included (message events only).

features.capability: Microsoft Teams task intake and status updates
features.lt: Real Teams does not sign bot-framework webhooks; the bearer-HMAC scheme is a documented adapter simplification (secret webhook URL or fronting proxy), swap point is the SignatureScheme row in teams.py.
Live linear.app not hit; GraphQL fake validates request shape only.
Real Jira webhooks are unsigned too — X-Jira-Secret is a documented adapter simplification (Atlassian Connect JWT is the future real scheme).
sentry.io not hit live; payload shape mirrors the documented webhook contract.

PARTIAL by honesty rule: Datadog's DEFAULT webhook payload shape (alert_title/alert_type/aggregation_key) is NOT parsed; Datadog requires configuring a custom payload template matching the implemented contract, which is documented in README but not itself validated against a live Datadog account. Grafana=complete, Datadog=via-templated-payload.
Push-only export; endpoint/TLS/auth are collector-side deployment concerns, no live production collector exercised here. Span set covers the frozen vocabulary only.
Quality is event-derived acceptance/rework/blocked/abandonment; review issue text is displayed but not semantically scored. UI is a minimal HTML page, not a product-grade frontend.
Measures the harness timeline (plan/approve/execute/review/PR) only; human context work outside runs is invisible. Deliberately NO per-developer score — metrics are per-run/team.
Depends on provider cost-ledger completeness (missing rows understate cost, never overstate). Infra/storage/human-review costs are out of scope.
Same clock source assumed for plan/pr timestamps (all events carry ts from one store); cross-service clock skew not normalized.
Single-node SQLite; q is a LIKE scan (pilot scale, not a search cluster). No archive UI beyond the table view; export API not included.
Event-derived coverage: evidence is only as complete as the telemetry archive it exports. Zip is generated on demand in-process; very large exports are not streamed.

features.capability: Alerts for stalled, risky, expensive, or policy-violating runs
features.lt: No muting/acknowledge API; resolution is state-driven (condition clears). Thresholds are deployment constants, not per-team config.
Cost numbers inherit provider cost-ledger coverage (missing rows understate). No CSV/PDF export, no per-day time series yet.
Webhook parsing covers push/pipeline failure events, not every provider event type. No provider-side app installation flow (config is env-driven).

features.capability: Chat notifications with approve, reject, and inspect actions
features.lt: Slack app installation/config is operator-owned; no Slack Block Kit UI shipped (payloads only). Reject is a recorded note until a reject route exists.
No calendar (CalDAV/Google) two-way sync — this is schedule-as-data with an operator cron sweep documented in runbook.md. No per-schedule retry backoff beyond claim release.
